name: ROADrecon - Offline Azure AD / Entra ID Enumeration
description: ROADrecon (part of ROADtools) authenticates to Entra ID and dumps the entire directory into a local SQLite database, then serves an offline GUI and BI/analysis of users, groups, roles, applications, service principals, devices, and OAuth2 permission grants. Enables deep offline Azure AD recon and privilege-path analysis after a single collection.
notes:
=== AUTHENTICATE ===
  roadrecon auth -u <user> -p <password>
  # Device code flow:
  roadrecon auth --device-code
  # With a refresh token:
  roadrecon auth --refresh-token "<refresh_token>"
  # As a service principal:
  roadrecon auth -c <app_id> --as-app -p "<client_secret>" -t <domain>

=== GATHER THE DIRECTORY (-> roadrecon.db SQLite) ===
  roadrecon gather
  roadrecon gather --mfa        # include MFA/auth method data

=== OFFLINE GUI ===
  roadrecon gui
  # Browse users/groups/roles/apps/SPs/devices/OAuth grants at http://127.0.0.1:5000

=== PLUGINS / ANALYSIS ===
  roadrecon plugin policies      # dump Conditional Access policies
  roadrecon plugin road2timeline  # activity timeline

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
  - Users/SPs with directory/privileged roles
  - App registrations with secrets + high permissions
  - OAuth2PermissionGrants (illicit consent)
  - Dynamic group rules (self-add escalation)

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  AzureHound     # BloodHound graph format
  Stormspotter   # ARM + AAD
  az cli / Graph # targeted queries

recommended.note: AzureHound produces BloodHound-graph output instead of SQLite.
Targeted Entra enumeration for specific objects.

defense.why_it_works: ROADrecon calls the internal Azure AD Graph/Microsoft Graph with a normal user or SP token. Default directory read permissions let any principal enumerate most of the tenant into an offline copy.
defense.prerequisites: Any valid Entra credential or token; network to login.microsoftonline.com and Graph.
defense.impact: Full offline copy of the tenant directory enabling privilege-path and misconfiguration analysis.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1087.004] Bulk Graph/AAD Graph reads from one principal; ROADrecon/ROADtools client identifiers; device-code auth from unusual locations.
defense.artifacts: Entra sign-in logs with ROADtools client; high-volume directory reads; a roadrecon.db on the attacker host.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=azure sourcetype=azure:signin OR sourcetype=azure:graph
| stats count by user, appDisplayName
| where count > 500
defense.sentinel_kql:
SigninLogs
| where AppDisplayName has "ROADtools" or UserAgent has "roadrecon"
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, AppDisplayName
defense.prevention: Least-privilege roles; restrict directory read and guest access; Conditional Access to block legacy/unknown clients and risky sign-ins; monitor bulk Graph reads; disable device-code flow where unused.
